plants.name: Cuban oregano
plants.description: Bring bold flavor to your kitchen with this fragrant herb’s thick, velvety leaves. Finely chop a little into chicken marinades, savory meat dishes or stuffing; its strong aroma means a small amount goes a long way. A handy choice for a patio herb pot, with partial shade and well-drained soil.

care.water: Water periodically; avoid keeping the roots soggy.

photo.alt: Illustration of a young cuban oregano in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

largerPhoto.alt: Illustration of a larger cuban oregano in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

plants.name: Spearmint
plants.description: Pick a few sweet-smelling leaves for fresh mint tea, lemonade or fruit salad. Spearmint also brightens yogurt sauces and makes a refreshing garnish for desserts and cold drinks. Keep a pot near the kitchen for easy snipping; give it some afternoon shade and evenly moist soil, with its own container to keep the runners contained.

care.sun: Sun to partial shade; some afternoon shade helps in Florida.
care.soil: Moist, well-drained soil; a container helps control spreading.

photo.alt: Illustration of a young spearmint in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

largerPhoto.alt: Illustration of a larger spearmint in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

plants.name: Sweet potato
plants.description: Grow more than a side dish: sweet potatoes offer roots for roasting, mashing and baking, plus tender young leaves you can cook as greens. Their trailing vines add a lush look to an edible garden while the crop develops below ground. Give them sun, loose soil and room to spread; roots need a growing season before harvest.

care.water: Water during establishment and dry periods; avoid soggy soil.
care.soil: Loose, well-drained soil with room for roots and vines.

photo.alt: Illustration of a young sweet potato in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

largerPhoto.alt: Illustration of a larger sweet potato in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

plants.name: Banana
plants.description: Bring a tropical feel to your yard with big, lush leaves that make a striking backdrop for an edible garden. Mature banana leaves can be used as cooking wraps for steaming or grilling, helping hold moisture around the food. Plant in a warm, sunny, wind-protected spot and water regularly to support strong growth.

care.sun: Full sun in a wind-protected spot.
care.water: Water regularly; keep moist without leaving the soil continuously wet.

photo.alt: Illustration of a young banana in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

largerPhoto.alt: Illustration of a larger banana in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

plants.name: Tice mulberry
plants.description: Enjoy sweet, juicy mulberries fresh, spooned over yogurt or cooked into homemade jam. A Tice mulberry adds a fruit-tree centerpiece to an edible yard, with berries worth making room for. Plant away from patios where fallen fruit could stain. Extra-large trees beyond these two size options are priced individually.

care.water: Water while establishing; established trees tolerate drier conditions.
care.soil: Well-drained soil with space for a tree to develop.

photo.alt: Illustration of a young tice mulberry in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

largerPhoto.alt: Illustration of a larger tice mulberry in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

plants.name: Fig
plants.description: Grow tree-ripened figs for fresh snacks, breakfast bowls and homemade preserves. Their soft, sweet fruit also pairs beautifully with cheese or a simple salad, while broad leaves give the garden a distinctive look. Choose a sunny spot with well-drained soil; a fig can be trained as a small tree or a bush as it grows.

care.water: Provide consistent moisture; avoid excessively wet soil.
care.soil: Well-drained soil; mulch helps retain moisture.

photo.alt: Illustration of a young fig in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

largerPhoto.alt: Illustration of a larger fig in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

plants.name: Passion fruit
plants.description: Turn a sunny trellis into a leafy feature with intricate flowers and fruit prized for its fragrant, tangy pulp. Spoon ripe pulp into yogurt, blend it into drinks or use it in desserts and homemade jam. Give this vigorous climber sturdy support and regular water, and train its stems along a fence or trellis as it grows.

care.sun: Full sun for best flowering and fruiting.
care.water: Keep moisture consistent; avoid drought and waterlogging.
care.soil: Well-drained soil; provide a trellis for the climbing vine.

photo.alt: Illustration of a young passion fruit in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

largerPhoto.alt: Illustration of a larger passion fruit in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

plants.name: Turmeric
plants.description: Grow the golden spice you can grate fresh into curries, rice, soups or smoothies. Turmeric brings earthy flavor and rich yellow color to cooking, while its broad tropical leaves add interest to a partly shaded garden. Plant in rich, well-drained soil and keep it moist during growth; harvest the rhizomes as the foliage dies back at season’s end.

care.soil: Rich soil with organic matter and good drainage.

photo.alt: Illustration of a young turmeric in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

largerPhoto.alt: Illustration of a larger turmeric in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

plants.name: Sugarcane
plants.description: Grow a sweet taste of the tropics with tall, leafy canes that sway in the breeze. Mature stalks can be pressed for fresh sugarcane juice, enjoyed in cold drinks or cooked down into syrup. The upright foliage adds height to an edible garden; give the clump a sunny spot with room to grow, away from narrow paths.

care.water: Keep new plants moist without drowning the roots.
care.soil: Well-drained soil; allow room away from paths.

photo.alt: Illustration of a young sugarcane in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

largerPhoto.alt: Illustration of a larger sugarcane in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

plants.name: Moringa
plants.description: Grow a leafy ingredient for your kitchen on a fast-growing tree. Young moringa leaves can be cooked into soups, stirred into rice or prepared as greens, making it a useful addition to an edible garden. Regular pruning helps keep new growth within reach; give it a sunny spot and freely draining soil.

care.sun: Sun; protect new cuttings while they establish.
care.water: Avoid prolonged wetness; let the medium drain freely.

photo.alt: Illustration of a young moringa in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.

largerPhoto.alt: Illustration of a larger moringa in a charcoal pot against a cream wall.
